# fitness

fitness runs a repo's fitness checks: small programs that each judge one rule, such as spelling, tests, or pull request shape. Each check is its own program installed from fitness-checks, the engine judges local-branch itself, and a repo may add local checks. Each check decides whether it applies, so any repo runs the same suite with nothing to configure.

A run resolves the checks, runs them side by side under two totals, and prints a table of passed, failed, or info results. Info never fails a run. With files staged it judges only those files; --all judges every tracked file.

## Exit codes

- 0: every check passed, or a command succeeded.
- 1: a check found problems, or the run could not start, such as a bad config.
- 2: a command got arguments it does not take, or explain or docs named an unknown check or topic.

## Learn the rest

`fitness list` names every check, `fitness explain <check>` says why one exists and how to pass it, and `fitness docs` serves the guides. All of them, and this page, come from the code's own doc comments.

## Run checks

- `fitness` or `fitness <check> [args]`: Runs the full suite, or with a check name only that check, passing it the arguments after its name.
- `fitness --all`: Forces a full scan even when files are staged.
- `fitness --blob <text>`: Runs every blob-capable check on a text instead of the repo; - reads the text from stdin.
- `fitness --dir=<folder>`: Judges only the files under one folder.
- `fitness --file=<path>`: Judges only the named file; repeat it to name more.
- `fitness --json=<file>`: Names the file that receives the run's performance report: each check's time, stage, files, binary size, and error lines, as JSON.
- `fitness --no-builtins [args]`: Turns the built-in checks off, so a run uses only installed checks, as a clean install would; it comes first.
- `fitness --policy=external --checks=<name,name>`: Select the checks a command line names: with --policy=external, a run runs exactly the checks --checks lists.

## Commands

- `fitness llms`: Prints a page that teaches an AI the whole CLI.
- `fitness list [--json]`: Names every check with its summary, scope, stage, and whether this repo enables it.
- `fitness check-versions`: Prints each check the repo installs with its version pin, as checkVersions in .fitnessrc.json sets them.
- `fitness explain <check> [--json]`: Prints why a check exists, what it judges, and the config keys it reads.
- `fitness docs [topic]`: Lists the guide topics, or prints one, from the code's doc comments.
- `fitness check --list` or `fitness check <name> [args]`: Prints each check the engine runs itself, one per line, or runs one check by name, installed or the repo's own.
- `fitness config [--json] [--policy=..] [--checks=..]` or `fitness config schema`: Shows the resolved settings and each check's state, or prints a JSON Schema for the config file.
- `fitness init`: Installs the shared git hooks into this repo.
- `fitness hook <name>`: Runs a git hook: commit-msg, pre-commit, or pre-push.
- `fitness boxes <report.json> <page.html>`: Draws a --json report as an HTML box diagram.
- `fitness perf <report.json>`: Prints each check's duration from a --json report, slowest first.
- `fitness strip-front-matter`: Deletes the fitness keys from tracked Markdown files' front matter, and any block they leave empty.
- `fitness adr-migrate [--dry-run] [--repo=owner/name] [--branch=main]`: Moves each ADR file into an `ADR` issue and points its links there.
- `fitness comments [path...]`: Prints each code comment block of the tracked files, or of those under the named paths, with its line, language and kind.
- `fitness branch-check`: Judges this branch's PR and the issues it closes locally, posting nothing.
- `fitness pr-check`: Judges pull request titles and descriptions, in GitHub Actions.
- `fitness dependabot-pr`: Completes a Dependabot pull request so pr-check judges it like a person's, in GitHub Actions.
- `fitness issue-check`: Judges an issue by its kind label and comments the result, in GitHub Actions.
- `fitness plan-check`: Judges Plan issues only, as issue-check does, in GitHub Actions.
- `fitness close-check`: Reopens an issue closed with unchecked items, or closes the parent it finishes, in GitHub Actions.
- `fitness dupe-check`: Notes when a new issue resembles an older one, in GitHub Actions.
- `fitness comment-check --blob <text>` or `fitness comment-check`: Judges a drafted comment, where - or no text reads stdin, or judges issue and PR comments and reply, in GitHub Actions.
- `fitness claude-hook`: Judges what a Claude Code hook event on stdin names.

## Checks

`fitness explain <check>` prints a check's whole documentation.

- `local-branch`: Runs PR and Plan judgments locally.

## Topics

- `fitness docs config`: Package conf loads .fitnessrc.json — the Go runner's configuration file.
- `fitness docs coverage`: Package goal holds the coverage goal every coverage check judges by, whichever language it measures: every counted line, branch or statement covered.
- `fitness docs github`: cspell:ignore approv aproved dont doesnt didnt cant wont isnt wasnt arent
- `fitness docs hooks`: Package hooks embeds the canonical may-journal git hooks that `fitness init` installs into a consumer repo.
- `fitness docs languages`: Package lang defines what a language module brings to a run and orders what modules claim against what is installed or embedded.
- `fitness docs local-checks`: Package repocheck finds a repo's own checks (ADR 0009, ADR 0012) and builds the Go ones, as docs/local-checks.md describes.
- `fitness docs protocol`: Package checkkit is the contract between the fitness runner and a check binary, which prints one JSON Result on stdout.
